In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study found that the major modifiable risk factor for the burden of disease in 2009 was smoking followed by high blood pressure and high blood cholesterol, and that the burden attributable to high BMI and alcohol use was increasing.

the burden of disease and injury in Thailand is high and increasing, and that the main contributors to this burden are the modifiable risk factors of tobacco smoking, high blood pressure (hypertension), high blood cholesterol (hypercholesterolaemia), high body mass index, and harmful use of alcohol.

Thailand has made significant progress in reducing the burden of communicable diseases, however, there are still a large proportion of deaths and DALYs due to non-communicable diseases (NCDs), and the burden is increasing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the health burden attributable to the major modifiable risk factor is high and that there is an urgent need to reduce this burden.

the most important modifiable risk factors for health in Thailand in 2010 were tobacco use (especially for males), high BMI, high systolic blood pressure, harmful alcohol use, high total cholesterol and low fruit and vegetable intake (especially for females).

the burden of disease and injury attributable to modifiable health risk factors in Thailand in 2010 was 3.4 million disability adjusted life years and that the top four health risks were high BMI, tobacco smoking, high blood pressure and alcohol consumption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the harmful use of tobacco, high blood pressure high blood cholesterol, high body mass index and alcohol use account for a large proportion of the disease burden in Thailand.
the burden of disease in the country is largely due to modifiable risk exposures, which means that the country is able to prevent a significant proportion of disease and disability.
the burden attributable to tobacco and alcohol use and high BMI, blood pressure, and cholesterol is substantial in Thailand, especially among men.
